children: Taiwan's August exports likely rose 33.85% from a year earlier, according to a Wall Street Journal poll of six economists. That would be slightly stronger than July's 32.9% but down from June's 40.3%. Taiwan's hardware makers, led by TSMC, have become the backbone of the artificial-intelligence infrastructure build-out and boosted the island's advanced tech exports. However, Taiwan's export momentum has slowed in recent months from peak growth of more than 60% earlier this year. DBS economists reckon that the U.S.-led AI investment boom appears to be transitioning from a supercycle to a more steady cycle as high base effects emerge, global interest rates rise and regulatory uncertainties increase. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
